headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear the costs of their increased electricity generating capacity and distribution infrastructure, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed HB 1393, requiring facilities using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity and preventing these costs from being passed to other customers. Governor Spanberger also urged the SCC to require data centers to pay for transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their operations, saving residential families hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers monthly, enhancing transparency and enabling better management of water resources.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Pass Data Center Water Reporting Requirements
news_summary: SB 553, along with HB 496, requires water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers each month, giving the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality better information for water resource decisions. This legislation aims to bring transparency to data center water use, which can be millions of gallons daily.

headline: Local Data Center Siting, Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill establishes a new permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Siting Assessments, Noise Studies
news_summary: HB 153 establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (100 MW or more), requiring zoning applicants to conduct site assessments for sound profiles near homes and schools. It also allows localities to require assessments of potential impacts on water resources, agriculture, and historic sites.
